primary_claim: Visually pre-marking one multiple-choice answer option (bubbling, highlighting, or enlarging it) systematically biases vision-language model responses toward that option even when it contradicts the correct answer, with susceptibility varying strongly across models: Gemini-1.5-flash is most susceptible (up to ~45 percentage-point response shifts and up to 23-point accuracy drops) while LLAVA-1.5-7b and Claude-haiku are most resilient.

effect.metric: shift in answer-selection rate toward pre-marked option (percentage points), and accuracy change
effect.value: Gemini-1.5-flash: +30.06 to +44.98 pp shift, up to -23.18 pp accuracy drop; Claude-haiku: up to +20 pp shift, -7 to 0 pp accuracy change; GPT-4o-mini: intermediate, variable accuracy impact; LLAVA: shifts not statistically significant (paired t-test)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Extends Shtedritski et al.'s CLIP keypoint-localization visual prompting method (originally for referring expression comprehension) to a broader range of VLMs including GPT-4o-mini, Claude-haiku, Gemini-1.5-flash, and LLAVA-1.5-7b
stated_future_work: Test these concepts across an even more diverse set of architectures and configurations
Develop more comprehensive practical interventions (e.g. jailbreak mitigation strategies) and assess their effectiveness in real-world scenarios
Determine empirically and theoretically whether systematic multimodal bias is additive or subtractive
Extend the analysis to modalities beyond vision and text, such as audio or sensor data
Investigate whether findings translate to free-text generation tasks or other forms of human-AI interaction
limitations_stated: Scope of models tested is limited; generalizability could be enhanced with a broader range of state-of-the-art models
Primary focus was on measuring the bias rather than proposing jailbreak mitigation strategies
Token probability delta as a bias metric is still in early stages; unclear whether systematic bias is additive or subtractive

Infrastructure to study internal mechanisms (activation/attribution patching, max-activating dataset analysis, causal scrubbing) in VLMs is underdeveloped, and non-uniform VLM architectures complicate this
Study has not explored modalities other than vision and text
quote: We find a clear shift in the models' responses towards the pre-marked option across different architectures despite their previous correct answers.
